name: tau-banking-memory-cohort-01
first_release: Exactly the earliest graded archived source draw of each of the 45 development tasks with an available trajectory. The choice ignores success, source length, document returns and note content. At one reader repetition this is 225 writes and 450 full consultations with zero new first passes. Its sealed cells count toward the total. Authorization for the first release only does not authorize the remaining cells.

release_check.rule: Review the first release before scaling. Verify source, bank, opening and grade seals. The grade and uptake thresholds guide the spending recommendation; five different tasks express breadth, not statistical significance. Authorization determines what is funded. The sign or magnitude of success differences does not determine the check. A different policy needs separate registration and reporting.

design: Use every officially graded draw of both outcomes in the registered groups. Reuse the 132 graded development draws and retain all six historical technical misses. Assign three fresh first passes on each of the 48 other tasks. Include successes, failures, incomplete tasks and all observed difficulty patterns. The first pass uses the original native task. The writer sees only the public trajectory and one binary result, without task tags, reference actions, answer keys or future messages. Each writer must store a nonempty memory. Give its exact sealed bank to both deliveries in separate sessions of the same task and opening. Start eligible siblings when one form is technically missing. No second-pass no-memory or substitution.
delivery: Preload uses the shared neutral memory notice and the assigned bank at session start. On demand retains the exact first-pass system message and business tools and only adds the contextual list/get tool descriptions of the pinned interface. The model decides whether to open them. Validate wire messages, native database, model settings and the recorded first public customer message before dispatch.
primary: For each bank compare automatically provided versus optional tool retrieval by official success. Pair on the same task, source draw, form and reader repetition. Report wins, losses, ties, missing and an equal-customer, equal-task weighted difference with exact customer sign test and missing-data bounds; separately show the 16 confirmation tasks of 11 known new customers. Development includes previous tasks, with unknown identities explicitly grouped by task for descriptive comparisons. Five form tables are exploratory.
secondary: Each condition versus its own first-pass outcome: recoveries, regressions and shared successes with token, request and cost differences. Count dispatched reader requests containing title or body, distinguish retrieval attempts and returns from actual input exposure, and preserve run/snapshot/journal references. Report completion and confirmed/held charges by stage. Outcome transitions do not attribute individual successes to memory.
spending: The separate first-pass screen is sunk. All new source, writer and reader charges and unresolved holds share one new ceiling. New requests require separate user authorization tied to the cohort and repeat count. On interruption resume only unstarted assignments. Terminal attempted failures stay missing; no outcome-dependent replacements.
